info.name: Techtrackers API v1
info.description:
Technical Support Logging System - Node.js / Express / PostgreSQL backend.

## Before you start
1. Start the API:  cd server && npm run dev
2. Import BOTH this collection and `Techtrackers.postman_environment.json`.
3. Select the **Techtrackers Local** environment (top-right dropdown).
4. Run **01 Auth > Login (Admin)** first - it saves the token automatically.

## How the automation works
Requests write variables ({{accessToken}}, {{logId}}, ...) into the environment via their
Tests scripts, so later requests reuse them without any copy-pasting. Run the folders
top to bottom, or use the Collection Runner on the whole collection.

Every request has assertions in its **Tests** tab - the green/red result IS the verification.

item.name: 00 Health & Index
item.description: Confirm the API and its database are reachable before anything else.

request.description:
Returns 200 when the API is up AND Postgres answers a query; 503 if the database is unreachable.

VERIFY: `database` reads "connected".
Self-describing directory of every mounted route group.

item.name: 01 Auth
item.description:
Sign-in, token refresh and password reset.

The old C# API had NO authentication at all - login returned a JSON blob and every other
endpoint was wide open. Everything here is new.

request.description:
RUN THIS FIRST.

Returns an access token (15 min) + refresh token (7 days).
The Tests tab saves both to the environment, so every later request is authenticated automatically.

VERIFY: `data.user.roles` contains "ADMIN"; `data.accessToken` is a 3-part JWT.
A second identity, used later to prove role-based access control actually blocks things.

VERIFY: the message is exactly the same as for an unknown email - "Invalid email or password".
Anything more specific would tell an attacker which addresses have accounts.

exec: pm.test("no account enumeration", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql("Invalid email or password"));

request.description: Compare this response body with the previous one. They must be byte-identical.
Validation runs BEFORE the controller. VERIFY: `errors[]` names the offending field.

Identity comes from the TOKEN, never from a URL parameter.
This is the fix for the old `/GetAdminLoggedIssues/admin/{adminId}` pattern, where changing the number in the URL read someone else's data.

Exchanges a refresh token for a fresh access token AND a new refresh token (rotation).

VERIFY: run this twice. The second run returns 401 because the first rotation revoked the old token - that is how token theft is detected.

Expect 400: the new password must differ from the current one.
Change `newPassword` to something else to see it succeed - note that it signs you out of all devices.

Sends a 6-digit code.

WITH NO SMTP CONFIGURED the code is printed to the API's console instead of emailed - look at the terminal running `npm run dev` for a line like:
  [MAIL:CONSOLE] To: ... Your Techtrackers one-time code is 123456.

VERIFY: try an email that does not exist. You still get 200 with the same message - no account enumeration.

Paste the real code from the console into `code`.
As written (000000) it returns 400 - and each wrong attempt is counted, so a 6-digit code cannot be brute-forced.

Paste the real code into `code`.

VERIFY afterwards:
  1. Login with the NEW password -> 200
  2. Login with the OLD password -> 401
  3. Reusing the same code -> 400 (codes are single-use)
  4. Try newPassword "weak" -> 422 listing every unmet rule

Revokes the refresh token. Omit the body to sign out of EVERY device.

Run 'Login (Admin)' again afterwards to continue testing.

item.name: 02 Reference Data
item.description:
Departments, categories and SLA targets. Any signed-in user may READ them (the ticket form
needs the dropdowns); only ADMIN may write.

The old system had no category endpoints at all, and no way to configure SLAs through the API
despite SLA being its headline feature.

request.description:
Populates the category dropdown on the log-an-issue form.
Saves the first id as {{categoryId}} for later requests.
VERIFY: each row carries a `code` (ICT, HR, FIN...). That code becomes the ticket reference prefix, e.g. HR-0001.

THE AUTOMATED SLA TABLE. One row per priority; a new ticket's priority selects its row and its deadlines.

VERIFY: CRITICAL responds in 15 min / resolves in 240 min; LOW is 480 / 4320.
VERIFY: POST the same name twice -> 409 Conflict (unique constraint translated to the right status, not a 500).
THE RBAC PROOF. Same URL, same body, non-admin token -> 403.

Upsert: posting an existing priority UPDATES it rather than failing.

VERIFY: set responseMinutes larger than resolutionMinutes -> 400, because you cannot be given longer to acknowledge than to fix.

Reference data attached to real tickets cannot be deleted.
The old DeleteDepartment called Remove() unconditionally and returned a raw SQL foreign-key error as a 500.

item.name: 03 Tickets - Create & Read
item.description:
The core of the system. Note that the reporter is taken from the TOKEN - there is no field in
the request that can name a different one (the old LogDto had `Staff_ID` in the body).

request.description:
THE HEADLINE FLOW - automated SLA assignment.

VERIFY in the response:
  - `data.reference` is like HR-0001 (department code + sequence, unique)
  - `data.status` is PENDING
  - `data.sla.priority` is HIGH - matched automatically from the priority you sent
  - `data.timestamps.responseDueAt` AND `resolutionDueAt` are BOTH already set

That last point is the fix: the old code left resolutionDue NULL until a background job
noticed the response deadline had passed, so an unassigned ticket had no deadline at all.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Laptop will not power on",
  "description": "My work laptop stopped powering on this morning after a Windows update installed overnight.",
  "categoryId": "{{categoryId}}",
  "priority": "HIGH",
  "location": "HR Office, 2nd floor"
}

exec: if (pm.response.code === 201) { const a = pm.response.json().data.attachments; pm.environment.set("attachmentLogId", pm.response.json().data.id); if (a.length) pm.environment.set("attachmentId", a[0].id); }

request.description:
Multipart upload. In Postman click the `attachments` row and choose real files.

VERIFY:
  - `data.attachments[]` lists name/type/size but NOT the file bytes
  - the files appear in `server/uploads/` with RANDOMISED names (a client cannot control the path on disk)
  - try a .sh or .exe -> 400, blocked by the mime allow-list
  - try a file over 5MB -> 400

The old API stored the raw bytes in the database and base64-inlined them into every list
response; a page of tickets with photos was tens of megabytes of JSON.

formdata.value: The external monitor at my desk flickers every few seconds since this morning.

formdata.description: Pick 1-5 files (images, PDF, docx, xlsx, txt). Max 5MB each.

request.description: VERIFY: `errors[]` lists EVERY failing field at once, not just the first.

VISIBILITY SCOPING - the same URL returns different data per role, decided from the JWT:
  STAFF      -> only tickets they reported
  TECHNICIAN -> only tickets assigned to them (or accepted collaborations)
  HOD        -> everything in their department
  ADMIN      -> everything

The old API took `isTechnician` as a QUERY-STRING BOOLEAN, so callers chose their own permissions.

VERIFY: compare `meta.total` here against the same request with {{adminToken}}.

Filters: status, priority, categoryId, departmentId, technicianId, open, overdue, search, sort.

Try `overdue=true` to list every ticket past its SLA deadline - a question the old API could not answer.
Case-insensitive match across title, description and reference.
Full detail: status history, escalations, feedback, attachment metadata and live SLA position.

item.name: Get a ticket you may NOT see (expect 404)

request.description:
A technician with no connection to this ticket gets 404 - NOT 403.
404 does not confirm the ticket exists, so ids cannot be probed.

(If tech2 was assigned or accepted a collaboration earlier in your run, this returns 200 - that is correct.)

One grouped query returns every status count plus open/overdue totals.
The old TechController needed five separate endpoints to draw four tiles.

item.name: Live SLA status of a ticket

request.description:
THE SLA COUNTDOWN, for a progress bar in the UI.

VERIFY the fields:
  percentConsumed          how much of the resolution window is used
  resolutionRemainingMinutes  negative once breached
  dueEscalationLevel       what the background job will act on (1 at 50%, 2 at 75%, 3 at 100%)
  responseBreached / resolutionBreached

The same pure function produces this and drives the escalation job, so what the user sees
and what the system acts on can never disagree.
Streams the file from disk with its original filename. Run the attachment upload request first.

item.name: 04 Assignment
item.description:
Dispatching work. ADMIN and HOD only.

The old version lived entirely inside a controller method and would assign ANY user id you
passed - including a staff member or a number that did not exist.

request.description:
VERIFY: each technician carries `openTaskCount` - their current workload - so assignment is an informed choice.
The old endpoint returned name and email only.

Recommends the least-loaded technician, preferring the reporter's own department.
Groundwork for true auto-assignment - it only recommends, a human still confirms.

VERIFY:
  - `data.status` becomes ASSIGNED
  - `data.timestamps.respondedAt` is stamped - THIS STOPS THE RESPONSE SLA CLOCK
  - the technician now receives a notification (check folder 08)
  - the technician can now GET the ticket (they got 404 before)

VERIFY: the message tells you how to proceed - send `reassign: true`.
The old code returned a flat 400 and offered NO way to ever change an assignment, so a mistake was permanent.
VERIFY: both the old and new technician are notified, and both workload counters are corrected in the same transaction.

THE CHECK THE OLD CODE NEVER MADE. It only tested `TechnicianId <= 0`.
VERIFY: the message names the roles the user actually holds.

item.name: 05 Ticket Lifecycle
item.description:
Status transitions. Run these IN ORDER - the point is that the lifecycle is enforced.

Legal transitions are declared as data in `src/constants/index.js`. The old API let any string
be written over any status, including reviving a CLOSED ticket.

request.description:
Uses tech2's token because the reassign step moved the ticket to them.

VERIFY: the reporter gets a notification; a row is added to the ticket's status history.

A business rule enforced in the SERVICE, so it holds no matter which route reaches it.
The old code had a note field for holds and silently ignored it when missing.

THE LIFECYCLE PROOF. You must come off hold before you can resolve.

VERIFY: the error message LISTS the legal next states.

VERIFY: `timestamps.resolvedAt` is stamped. Every report measures against THIS, not against the SLA deadline.

The old reports computed `ResolutionDue - AssignedAt` - the SLA WINDOW - so they showed the same
'average resolution time' whether a ticket was fixed in an hour or never fixed at all.

A technician with no connection to this ticket cannot drive it.
Only the assigned technician, an accepted collaborator, the reporter (to close a RESOLVED ticket),
an ADMIN, or the ticket's own HOD may change status.
The reporter confirms the fix worked. VERIFY: a reporter can NOT mark their own ticket RESOLVED - only CLOSE one already resolved by the technician.

CLOSED is terminal in the transition table, so reopening has its own endpoint and its own audit note.

VERIFY: `resolvedAt` is cleared, so reports no longer count it as solved.

EVERY transition, who made it, when, and why.

The LogStatusHistory table existed in the old schema and was NEVER WRITTEN TO - a ticket's past was unknowable.
Escalation independent of the SLA clock. VERIFY: an `escalations` row is written and the technician is alerted.

item.name: 06 Collaboration
item.description:
Technician-to-technician help requests.

The old endpoints took a technician id from the URL and no identity at all, so anyone could
accept anyone else's invitation - and accepting granted no actual access to the ticket.

request.description:
Only the ASSIGNED technician (or an admin) may invite others.
An email is also sent - visible in the API console when SMTP is not configured.
The old code allowed this happily.

`direction` = incoming | outgoing | all. Always scoped to YOU - no user id appears in the URL.
The old API needed two endpoints that each took a technician id and would happily return someone else's.

item.name: Requester tries to accept their own (expect 403)

request.description: THE FIX FOR THE BIGGEST HOLE HERE. Only the INVITED technician may respond.

VERIFY: after accepting, tech1 can GET the ticket (folder 03, 'Get a ticket you may NOT see').
Acceptance grants real visibility - in the old system it only changed a status column.
Only the requester (or an admin) may cancel, and only while still PENDING.

item.name: 07 Chat & Feedback
item.description:
Per-ticket conversation and satisfaction rating.

In the old stack the chat CONTROLLER saved messages and the SignalR HUB broadcast them - and
the two were never connected, so half your conversation vanished on refresh.

request.description:
Persisted AND broadcast over Socket.IO in one path.
Participants only: reporter, assigned technician, accepted collaborators, admins and HODs.

The old hub had NO authentication - anyone could join any ticket's conversation and post as anyone.

(Returns 201 if tech1 accepted the collaboration above - that is correct.)
VERIFY: messages sent over the websocket appear here too, and vice versa. One path, one source of truth.

RULES: only the reporter, only once, only after RESOLVED/CLOSED, rating 1-5.

The old endpoint took the rater's id FROM THE BODY with no checks at all - so anyone could post
unlimited 5-star ratings for anyone, which made the technician performance report meaningless.

item.name: 08 Notifications
item.description:
Everything here is implicitly YOURS - no endpoint takes a user id.

The old API had THREE notification controllers (one returning a hard-coded string) and its
live endpoint was `GET /{userId}/staged`, so you could read anyone's by changing the number.

exec: const d = pm.response.json().data; if (d.length) pm.environment.set("notificationId", d[0].id);

request.description:
VERIFY: after logging a ticket and having it assigned, the staff member has several -
logged, assigned, status changed. `meta.unreadCount` drives the badge in the UI.
A single cheap count - poll this rather than fetching the whole list.
Scoped by userId as well as id, so guessing an id achieves nothing.

item.name: 09 Reports
item.description:
Management information. ADMIN and HOD see the full picture; a technician sees their own.

Every report is measured against what ACTUALLY happened (`resolvedAt - createdAt`). The old
reports used `resolutionDue - assignedAt` - the SLA window - so their numbers were fiction.

request.description:
VERIFY the ON_HOLD figure is non-zero once you have held a ticket.
In the old code the writer stored "ONHOLD" and the report counted "On Hold", so this tile was permanently 0.
Row-per-ticket export. VERIFY each row carries `resolutionHours` (real elapsed time) and `metSla` (true/false).
Trend over time: total, resolved, still open, average resolution hours, SLA compliance %.

Per-technician scorecard: assigned, resolved, open, escalated, average resolution hours,
SLA compliance %, resolution rate % and average rating.

Two queries total regardless of headcount - the old version ran four subqueries PER TECHNICIAN.

THE HEADLINE METRIC - and one the old system could not produce at all despite storing SLA data.

Answers: are we meeting our SLAs, broken down by priority, and how many open tickets are breached right now?

Everything a technician dashboard needs in ONE call: counts by status, open/overdue totals,
average resolution hours, SLA compliance % and average rating.

The old TechController exposed five separate count endpoints and could produce none of the performance figures.
A technician may read their OWN stats. Try another technician's id with this token -> 403.
Average plus the full 1-5 star distribution.

item.name: 11 User Administration
item.description:
ADMIN only.

The old AddUserService.cs - the file meant to own this - was ENTIRELY COMMENTED OUT, so there
was no way to create a user through the API. Users had to be inserted by hand in SQL.

request.description:
Creates the user AND their technician profile in ONE transaction, so the two tables cannot disagree.

VERIFY: the response contains NO password field, and `technicianProfile` is populated.
VERIFY: `errors[]` lists every unmet rule at once - length, uppercase, number.
Postgres' unique constraint (P2002) is translated to a 409, not surfaced as a 500.
VERIFY: sending an EMPTY body returns 422 - an update that changes nothing is a mistake, not a success.

DEACTIVATES rather than deletes - a user is referenced by every ticket they touched, so deleting
would destroy real history. Also revokes all their sessions immediately.

VERIFY: deactivating a technician who still has OPEN tickets -> 409 telling you to reassign first.

item.name: 12 Error Handling
item.description:
Proof that EVERY failure comes back in the same JSON envelope with the right status code.
In the old API these produced HTML error pages or 500s with internal detail leaked in `details`.

request.description: VERIFY: JSON, not Express' default HTML page.
Send deliberately broken JSON. VERIFY: 400 'Request body is not valid JSON', not a 500.
